summary: The note describes "The Green Lungs Project," a community garden initiative started by neighbors Jane Hamilton and Mark Torres to reduce urban air pollution. It covers community organizing, education, transformation of vacant lots, business and school participation, the Clean Air Fest, awards, air quality monitoring with universities, and plans for expansion.
one_line: Neighbors Jane Hamilton and Mark Torres launched The Green Lungs Project, using community gardens to cut urban air pollution and engage residents.
key_facts: Since September 5th, 2023, local residents have developed community gardens to reduce pollution and promote clean air activities.
Jane Hamilton and Mark Torres, two neighbors, initiated "The Green Lungs Project" after noticing declining air quality approaching unhealthy levels, especially on hot summer days.
Hamilton and Torres organized the community through social media and community boards, and consulted environmental scientists and horticulturists on pollution-absorbing plants.
Weekend workshops led by experts and volunteers taught urban gardening, local ecosystems, and how plants contribute to cleaner air; children's activities were also organized.
Six months after inception, the vacant lot at the corner of Fifth Street and Park Avenue was transformed into a garden.
Plants such as English ivy, spider plants, and fruits and vegetables serve as natural air filters in the gardens.
On November 15th, 2023, several local businesses adopted the ideology, adding plant walls and rooftop gardens.
Students from Lincoln Elementary School, guided by teacher Susan Chao, won the city's "Greenest Classroom Award".
The first annual "Clean Air Fest" was held on February 10th, 2024, with local musicians, environmental tip booths, and organic local produce.
Hamilton and Torres received the "Environmental Heroes" award on April 22nd, 2024, Earth Day.
Partnerships with local universities installed air quality monitors in and around the gardens; preliminary reports showed reduced nitrogen dioxide and particulate matter.
Planned expansions include vertical gardens for apartment complexes and promoting eco-friendly transport such as bike-sharing programs.
